title: In the Shadow of Your Wings
superscription: For the choirmaster. To the tune of "Do Not Destroy." A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul into the cave.

verses.text: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy, for in You my soul takes refuge. In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter until the danger has passed.
I cry out to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me.
He reaches down from heaven and saves me; He rebukes those who trample me. Selah God sends forth His loving devotion and His truth.
My soul is among the lions; I lie down with ravenous beasts— with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.
They spread a net for my feet; my soul was despondent. They dug a pit before me, but they themselves have fallen into it! Selah
My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make music.
Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations; I will sing Your praises among the peoples.
For Your loving devotion reaches to the heavens, and Your faithfulness to the clouds.
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.

context.author: The title names David. In Book Two, Psalms 51-65 are all “of David,” and several titles tie them to events in his life.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: The title places it “when he fled from Saul into the cave,” either the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1) or the cave at En Gedi where Saul came in and David spared him (1 Samuel 24:1-7). “Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy, for in You my soul takes refuge. In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter until the danger has passed” (v.1). “My soul is among the lions” (v.4); his enemies dug a pit and fell into it (v.6). The refrain: “Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth” (vv.5, 11). Then David breaks into song: “My heart is steadfast, O God… Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn” (vv.7-8). “For Your loving devotion reaches to the heavens” (v.10).
context.custom: The limestone hills of Judah are full of caves used as shelters, hideouts and sheepfolds. Musicians woke at dawn to begin the morning praise; David says his song will wake the dawn itself. Do Not Destroy (title), the tune for Psalms 57-59 and 75, may be a known melody or a prayer in itself.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 58 calls unjust rulers to account.
context.timelineBible: Verses 7-11 appear again as the first half of Psalm 108. In the En Gedi cave David cut a corner off Saul’s robe instead of killing him, saying, “I will not lift my hand against my lord, since he is the LORD’s anointed” (1 Samuel 24:10). Paul and Silas sang hymns at midnight in prison (Acts 16:25).

gospelParallels.note: Paul and Silas singing at midnight.
As a hen gathers her chicks under her wings.
Sing and make music in your hearts to the Lord.

otBackground.note: David spares Saul in the cave at En Gedi.

overview.summary: Hiding from Saul in a cave among enemies like lions, David shelters under the shadow of God’s wings and ends by waking the dawn with praise.
overview.settingLine: A cave in the wilderness, before dawn.

archaeology.t: Caves in the cliffs above the springs.
Khirbet esh-Sheikh Madhkur, with caves nearby.

overview.discussion: David sings while still in the cave (vv.7-8). Can I praise God before my situation changes?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
